{{Short description|Genus of sauropod dinosaur}} {{Speciesbox | fossil_range =
[[Late Cretaceous]], late {{fossilrange|Maastrichtian|Maastrichtian|[[Maastrichtian]]}} | image = Phosphatotitan khouribgaensis (holotype, dorsal vertebra - drawing).png | image_caption = Holotype dorsal vertebra | image2 = Phosphatotitan khouribgaensis (holotype, caudal vertebra - drawing).png | image2_caption = Holotype tail vertebra | display_parents = 2 | genus = Phosphatotitan | parent_authority = Longrich et al., [[2026 in archosaur paleontology|2026]] | species = khouribgaensis | authority = Longrich et al., 2026 }} '''''Phosphatotitan''''' ({{lit|phosphate giant}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[titanosauria]]n sauropod dinosaur known from the [[Late Cretaceous]] ([[Maastrichtian]] age) [[Ouled Abdoun Basin]] of Morocco. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Phosphatotitan khouribgaensis''''', known from a partial skeleton. == Discovery and naming == [[File:Phosphatotitan khouribgaensis (locality).png|thumb|left|upright|Discovery locality of ''Phosphatotitan'']] The ''Phosphatotitan'' fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the Sidi Chennane [[Phosphate#Production|phosphate mine]] (Lower Couche III) of the [[Ouled Abdoun Basin]] in [[Khouribga Province]], Morocco. The specimen is housed in the Natural History Museum of Marrakech (''Muséum d'Histoire naturelle de Marrakech''), in [[Marrakech]], Morocco, where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen MHNM.KHG.888. The specimen consists of a fragmentary associated skeleton comprising some vertebrae (one {{dinogloss|dorsals|dorsal}} (trunk vertebra, a {{dinogloss|sacrum}} with at least four vertebrae, and one {{dinogloss|caudals|caudal}} (tail) vertebra) and parts of the pelvis (fragmentary {{dinogloss|ilium}}, both {{dinogloss|pubes}}, and possibly part of the {{dinogloss|ischium}}). [[Taphonomic]] damage to the specimen has resulted in it becoming cracked and crushed. In 2026, Nicholas R. Longrich and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Phosphatotitan khouribgaensis'' as a new genus and species of titanosaur based on these fossil remains, establishing MHNM.KHG.888 as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Phosphatotitan'', combines a reference to the Moroccan phosphate deposits from which the fossils were recovered, with the word "titan" ({{lit|giant}}), a common suffix for sauropod names, referencing the [[Titans|pre-Olympian gods]] of [[Greek mythology]]. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''khouribgaensis'', references the discovery of the holotype in Khouribga Province. == Description == [[File:Phosphatotitan khouribgaensis (holotype, pelvis).png|thumb|upright|Pelvic bones (pubes and possible ischium) of the holotype]] While ''Phosphatotitan'' is large in relation to the non-sauropod dinosaurs it coexisted with, it is significantly smaller than its closest relatives within the titanosaur clade [[Lognkosauria]], which include ''[[Patagotitan]]'', which is estimated to have been {{convert|30|-|40|m|ft}} long and {{convert|57|-|69|t|ST}} in weight. With a dorsal vertebral centrum height of {{convert|15.9|cm|in}}, the linear dimensions of the ''Phosphatotitan'' fossils are about 39.75% of those of ''Patagotitan''. As such, its weight can be calculated to be between {{convert|3.5|and|4.3|t|ST}}, around 6.3% of the mass of ''Patagotitan''. == Classification == [[File:Phosphatotitan khouribgaensis.png|thumb|[[Life restoration]]]] In their [[phylogenetic analyses]] using an updated version of the dataset of Pérez-Moreno et al. (2024), Longrich et al. (2026) recovered ''Phosphatotitan'' as the [[sister taxon]] to an unnamed Moroccan specimen from the Sidi Daoui locality. The South American ''[[Patagotitan]]'' and ''[[Argentinosaurus]]'' were recovered as successive outgroups to this African group, together forming the clade [[Argentinosauridae]]. These taxa are part of the larger clade [[Lognkosauria]], whose only other definitive members are also South American. These results are displayed in the [[cladogram]] below: {{clade |style=font-size:85%; line-height:85%; |{{clade |1=''[[Epachthosaurus]]'' |2={{clade |1={{clade |1=''[[Mnyamawamtuka]]'' |2={{clade |1=''[[Malawisaurus]]'' |2=''[[Rukwatitan]]'' }} }} |3={{clade |1=''[[Dreadnoughtus]]'' |2=''[[Tapuiasaurus]]'' |3={{clade |label1=[[Saltasauroidea]] |1={{clade hidden |1=[[Lirainosaurinae]] |2={{clade |1=''[[Alamosaurus]]'' |label2=[[Saltasauridae]] |2={{clade |1=[[Opisthocoelicaudiinae]] |2=[[Saltasaurinae]] }} }} }} |label3=[[Colossosauria]] |3={{clade |1={{clade |1=''[[Baurutitan]]'' |2={{clade |1=[[Rinconsauria]] |2={{clade |1=''[[Overosaurus]]'' |2={{clade |1=''[[Punatitan]]'' |2={{clade |1=''[[Trigonosaurus]]'' |2=[[Aeolosaurini]] }} }} }} }} }} |label3=[[Lognkosauria]] |sublabel3={{small|(Argentinosauria)}} |3={{clade |1=''[[Bonitasaura]]'' |2=''[[Chucarosaurus]]'' |3=''[[Drusilasaura]]'' |4=''[[Futalognkosaurus]]'' |5=''[[Notocolossus]]'' |6=''[[Puertasaurus]]'' |7=''[[Quetecsaurus]]'' |8={{clade |1=''[[Mendozasaurus]]'' |2=''[[Traukutitan]]'' }} |label9=[[Argentinosauridae]] |9={{clade |1=''[[Argentinosaurus]]'' |2={{clade |1=''[[Patagotitan]]'' |2={{clade |1='''''Phosphatotitan''''' |2=Sidi Daoui titanosaur }} }} }} }} }} }} }} }} }}|label1=[[Titanosauria]]}} == Palaeobiology == Longrich et al. (2026) suggested that the small size of ''Phosphatotitan'' in relation to other lognkosaurs may be due to either [[island dwarfism]] (in the event that Morocco was possibly separated from parts of the African continent), or conditions of environments during the latest Cretaceous, wherein smaller herbivore diversification was favored over that of giant taxa. This is seen in South America, where the most prevalent titanosaurs (e.g., [[saltasaurine]]s, [[rinconsaur]]s, and [[aeolosaurin]]s) are fairly small, while giant taxa are more rare. Similarly, Egyptian titanosaurs are small-bodied, though giant taxa from this region are not known. ==Palaeoecology== [[File:Late Maastrichtian dinosaurs from the Moroccan Phosphates.png|thumb|left|Dinosaurs from the Moroccan Maastrichtian phosphates, including ''Phosphatotitan'' and the unnamed Sidi Daoui titanosaur, center]] ''Phosphatotitan'' is known from the phosphates of the [[Ouled Abdoun Basin]] of central Morocco, which dates to the late [[Maastrichtian]] age, of the late [[Cretaceous]] period, shortly before the [[Chicxulub impact|Chicxulub asteroid impact]] and [[K-Pg boundary]], the point at which the dinosaurs and many other groups went extinct. The phosphates preserve a nearshore marine environment dominated by [[mosasaurs]], fish, and other marine animals. Dinosaurs are less common, but include diverse [[hadrosaurids]], including ''[[Ajnabia]]'', ''[[Minqaria]]'', and ''[[Taleta]]'', in addition to the [[abelisaurid]] theropod ''[[Chenanisaurus]]''. Unnamed, fragmentary specimens belonging to both of these clades have also been described. In addition to ''Phosphatotitan'', an additional unnamed [[titanosauria]]n is also known from the Sidi Daoui locality, preserving a partial hindlimb ({{dinogloss|femur}}, {{dinogloss|tibia}}, and {{dinogloss|fibula}})). == References == {{Reflist|refs= {{Cite journal |last1=Longrich |first1=Nicholas R. |last2=Pérez-Moreno |first2=Agustín |last3=Díez Díaz |first3=Verónica |last4=Pereda-Suberbiola |first4=Xabier |last5=Bardet |first5=Nathalie |last6=Jalil |first6=Nour-Eddine |date=2026-04-22 |title=A titanosaurian sauropod with South American affinities (Lognkosauria: Argentinosauridae) from the Late Maastrichtian of Morocco and evidence for dinosaur endemism in Africa |journal=Diversity |language=en |volume=18 |issue=5 |article-number=241 |doi=10.3390/d18050241 |issn=1424-2818 |doi-access=free}} {{Cite journal|last1=Pérez-Moreno |first1=A. |last2=Salgado |first2=L. |last3=Carballido |first3=J.
